image_description: A close-up photograph of two unripe figs hanging from a branch against a background of large green fig leaves. The fig on the left is darker, showing purple and brown hues, while the fig on the right is predominantly green with some purple shading. Both exhibit the characteristic pear-like shape tapering to a stem. The lighting appears natural, highlighting the smooth skin texture of the fruit and the veining of the leaves.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Both fruits clearly display the pear-shaped morphology. The coloration matches the description: one is green/purple, the other is dark purple/brown.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The geometry is correct; both fruits are broader at the bottom (distal end) and taper smoothly toward the pedicel attachment point.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The angle of the photograph shows the side and top (stem end) of the figs. The bottom tip (ostiole) is occluded by the curvature of the fruit and the viewing angle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Narrow stem end contrasting with broad rounded base.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The transition from the thick fruit body to the thin stem (pedicel) is clearly visible and anatomically correct for a fig.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Thin, easily bruised skin covering soft interior.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visual texture suggests thin skin. There are no signs of rigid, thick rinds. The slight color variations suggest the translucency typical of thin-skinned figs.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The figs are whole and intact. No cross-section is visible in the image.
